# Contributing

For an AI agent or a person changing this repo. Read it before your first edit.

## Why this file exists

`AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are the product: they load into every project the user opens, and the Antigravity rulebook built from `AGENTS.md` must stay under a 24,000-byte cap. Notes about developing this repo would cost tokens in every session, so they live here, never there.

## Sources and generated files

Edit the sources. Never hand-edit a generated file; regenerate it.

| Sources (edit these) | What they are |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | The tool-neutral rulebook |
| `roles/*.md` | The agent roles: the five core roles and the six review-panel roles (`review-*`) |
| `adapters/<tool>.mjs` + `adapters/<tool>.notes.md` | One adapter per tool, and its tool notes |
| `models.json` | Tier to model, per tool |
| `profiles/*.md` | Optional rulebook additions |
| `standards/*.md` | The coding-standards archive, one file per stack (format in `standards/README.md`) |
| `review/` | The review panel: procedure, explorer contract, lane checklists, calibration and metrics formats |
| `workflows/*.md`, `templates/` | The portable workflows (`/start`, `/draft-pr` and others) and the target-repo rulebook template |
| `orchestration/standards.md`, `orchestration/sprint.md` | The standards setup procedure and sprint mode |
| `skills/*/SKILL.md` | Claude Code skills (copied into `~/.claude/skills` by hand) |
| `commands/*.md` (hand-written ones) | Claude Code commands for the workflows; the review-panel commands are generated (below) |

| Generated (do not edit) | Written by |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md`, `agents/*.md`, `commands/pre-pr-review.md`, `commands/review-verdict.md`, `commands/calibration-report.md` | `node tools/orc.mjs sync` |
| `tests/golden/**` | `node tools/orc.mjs golden` |
| `dist/` (untracked) | `node tools/orc.mjs build` |

`node tools/orc.mjs check` names the source to edit when `CLAUDE.md` or an `agents/*.md` file is out of date. Rulebooks and Codex TOML agents carry a `generated by orc.mjs` marker on their first lines; Claude Code `agents/*.md` do not, to save tokens in every agent prompt.

## The edit loop

```
# 1. edit a source
node tools/orc.mjs sync      # regenerates CLAUDE.md and agents/*.md
node tools/orc.mjs golden    # regenerates tests/golden/<tool>/
git diff tests/golden        # review: is every change one you meant?
npm test
node tools/orc.mjs check     # watch the antigravity headroom line
```

`node tools/orc.mjs help` lists every command; `help <command>` lists its options. The full reference is `docs/cli.md`.

## Traps

- **The allow-list `.gitignore`.** `/*` ignores everything, then `!/` lines re-include named paths. A new top-level file is silently untracked until it gets a `!/` line. Check with `git check-ignore <path>`: no output means it can be tracked. (`git check-ignore -v` also prints the `!/` rule that re-includes a file, so output there does not mean ignored.)
- **Review tier.** Editing `AGENTS.md`, `roles/`, `adapters/*.notes.md`, `profiles/`, any `SKILL.md` (such as `skills/repo-standards/SKILL.md`), `standards/`, `orchestration/standards.md` or `orchestration/sprint.md` (or the generated `CLAUDE.md` and `agents/`) makes `node tools/orc.mjs review-tier` say `Full`: prompts count as product, not docs.
- **The board is another repo.** The board page code in `orchestration/board` is its own repo (Co0pDawg/Orc-Dashboard), not part of this one.
- **`tools/worklog`** is a Windows-only example with its own `tools/worklog/test.ps1`. Its tests assert US Eastern local times, so CI sets the runner to Eastern time first.
- **`models.local.json`** is untracked. `check` validates it, but builds and compares from `models.json` only; `sync` and `golden` read `models.json` only. `build`, `install`, `status` and `dispatch` use it.

## Adding or refreshing a standards entry

The archive in `standards/` feeds `node tools/orc.mjs standards apply`, which composes a project's `STANDARDS.md`.

- Follow the format in `standards/README.md`: the frontmatter fields, the section order, and a `## Review checklist` with `- [ ]` items.
- Cite primary sources only (language or vendor docs, official style guides, the linter's own docs). End every rule with `[n]`, the n-th URL in `sources`.
- Paraphrase: write every rule in your own words and never copy sentences from a source.
- No company, project or ticket names: the archive is public. A team's own rules go into its project through `apply --from`.
- When refreshing an entry, recheck its sources and update `reviewed`.
- Run `node tools/orc.mjs check`: it validates every entry (id matches the file name, kind, detect, requires, the reviewed date, citation range and the checklist). Then try `node tools/orc.mjs standards apply --repo <temp dir> --stack <id>`.

## Development clone vs the live setup

The repo is designed to be checked out as `~/.claude`, but you can develop in a separate clone.

- In a separate clone, `sync` writes the clone's `CLAUDE.md` and `agents/*.md` only. The live `~/.claude` is not updated.
- Compare the live copy with the clone: `node tools/orc.mjs status --tool claude-code --home <your home>`. It writes nothing; it reports each file as `same`, `differs`, `missing`, `stale` or `extra`, and exits 0 only when all are `same`.
- `node tools/orc.mjs install --tool claude-code --home <dir>` writes that copy. It is a dry run without `--apply`; with `--apply` it backs up every file it replaces. `--tool claude-code` always needs `--home`. Try it on a temp folder first.
- A Claude Code session opened in a development clone loads both the live `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the clone's `CLAUDE.md`. When they differ, the clone's copy is the one being edited.

## Where things are

- `tools/orc.mjs`: the CLI. Loads roles, models and adapters, builds each tool (`buildTool`), and dispatches the commands.
- `tools/lib/`: `frontmatter.mjs` (frontmatter, generated marker), `roles.mjs` (role parsing), `models.mjs` (models validation), `toml.mjs` (Codex TOML), `manifest.mjs` (install manifest, path safety), `text.mjs` (the one text reader), `help.mjs` (the help table), `brief.mjs`, `reviewtier.mjs`, `costlog.mjs`, `dispatch.mjs`, `hooks.mjs` (the method-tooling commands), `standards.mjs` (the standards archive, detect and apply), `calibration.mjs` and `metrics.mjs` (the review panel's calibration and metrics).
- `tests/orc.test.mjs`: goldens, roles, frontmatter, caps, `check`, `install`, rulebook hygiene.
- `tests/hardening.test.mjs`: option parsing, refusals, stale agents, YAML quoting, running through a junction, BOM and UTF-16 input, first differing line.
- `tests/manifest.test.mjs`: install manifest, re-install, `uninstall`, `status`, symlink and junction refusals.
- `tests/tooling.test.mjs`: `brief`, `review-tier`, `costlog`, `dispatch`, `hooks`, the board reminder, models validation, `golden`, `help`, the generated marker.
- `tests/standards.test.mjs`: `standards list`, `show`, `detect` and `apply`, and the archive validation in `check`.
- `tests/review-tools.test.mjs`: `calibration` and `metrics`.

## Keep the README and wiki current

Every pull request that changes what a user sees or does updates the README and the wiki as part of the same change, not in a later docs pass. That covers a command, a flag, a role, a workflow, a skill, a mode, an install or restore step, a supported tool, or a limit that is added, changed or removed.

- **README.md** is in this repo, so its edit goes in the same commit range as the change.
- **The wiki** is its own repo, `https://github.com/Co0pDawg/Orc-istration.wiki.git`. Clone it, edit the matching page (the Home page index says which page covers what), add any new page to `_Sidebar.md` and the Home page index, and keep the `Next: [[...]]` chain unbroken. Push the wiki once the pull request merges, so the wiki never describes unmerged work.
- **The pull request description** carries a Docs line: the README sections and wiki pages updated, or `no user-facing change`. The pull request template asks for it.
- **Reviewers and refuters** treat a stale README section or wiki page as a must-fix, the same as a stale `docs/cli.md` entry.
- Evidence drawn from cost logs or other projects is anonymised before it goes in either place: the repo and the wiki are public.

## Pull requests

Branch off `main` and open a draft pull request against `main`. Fill in the template's Docs checklist (see "Keep the README and wiki current"). CI runs `npm test` and `node tools/orc.mjs check` on Ubuntu and Windows, plus the worklog test on Windows.
